questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will the tourists visit the desert during summer?

options.text: Has the desert been visited by the tourists during summer?
Is the desert visited by the tourists during summer?
Was the desert visited by the tourists during summer?
Will the desert be visited by the tourists during summer?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the desert be visited by the tourists during summer?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Future Simple Tense**. The active structure is: **Will** + **Subject** (the tourists) + **Base Verb** (visit) + **Object** (the desert) + **Adjunct** (during summer)?

• To convert a **Future Simple** interrogative sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure used is: **Will** + **New Subject** (the desert) + **be** + **Past Participle** (visited) + **by** + **New Object** (the tourists)?

• In the passive transformation, the **Object** of the active sentence (**the desert**) becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence.

• The **Subject** of the active sentence (**the tourists**) becomes the agent in the passive sentence, preceded by the preposition **by**.

• The verb **visit** is changed to its **third form** or **past participle**, which is **visited**, and is preceded by the auxiliary **be** to satisfy the **future passive** requirement.

• The time phrase **during summer** remains unchanged in its position as it functions as an **adverbial adjunct**.

 **Additional Information__**

• Understanding the incorrect options based on **Tense**:

• **Has the desert been visited...** is the **Present Perfect Passive** form, which is used for completed actions with relevance to the present.

• **Is the desert visited...** is the **Simple Present Passive** form, typically used for universal truths or habitual actions.

• **Was the desert visited...** is the **Simple Past Passive** form, used for actions that were completed at a specific time in the past.

• The original sentence uses **will**, indicating a **future intention** or **prediction**, therefore the passive must maintain the **Future Simple** construction using **will + be + V3**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The guests were being served refreshments by the hotel staff when the programme began.

options.text: The hotel staff served refreshments to the guests when the programme began.
The hotel staff were serving refreshments to the guests when the programme began.
The hotel staff had served refreshments to the guests when the programme began.
The hotel staff serve refreshments to the guests when the programme began.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The hotel staff were serving refreshments to the guests when the programme began.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Past Continuous Tense**, as indicated by the auxiliary structure **were being served** followed by the past participle of the verb.
 
• In the **Past Continuous Tense**, the **Passive Voice** structure is: **Object + was/were + being + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject**.
 
• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the structure must follow: **Subject + was/were + V1 + ing (Present Participle) + Object**.
 
• The **Passive Subject** (The guests) becomes the **Active Object**, and the **Passive Agent** introduced by **by** (the hotel staff) becomes the **Active Subject**.
 
• The verb phrase **were being served** is converted to its active continuous form **were serving** to maintain the ongoing nature of the action in the past.
 
• The time-identifying subordinate clause **when the programme began** remains unchanged as it provides the necessary context for the main action.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Continuous Tense Characteristics**:
 
 
• It describes an action that was **in progress** at a specific time in the past or when another action took place.
 
• In active sentences with a **Collective Noun** or plural subject like **hotel staff**, the plural auxiliary **were** is used for agreement.
 
• The conversion ensures that the **Transitive Verb** (serve) correctly links the subject to the **Direct Object** (refreshments) and **Indirect Object** (the guests).
 
 
 
• **Distinction from Other Tenses**:
 
 
• **Simple Past** (served) would imply a completed action rather than one that was **being performed**.
 
• **Past Perfect** (had served) would suggest the action was finished **before** the programme started, altering the original meaning.
 
• **Simple Present** (serve) is grammatically incorrect here as it violates the **tense consistency** required by the past-tense clause **began**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The CEO decided to quit the job _______ several reasons.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**for**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The preposition '**for**' is used to indicate a **purpose**, **reason**, or **cause**. 
• In the given sentence, the **CEO** is quitting the job, and the phrase following the blank ('**several reasons**') explains **why** he made that decision. 
• The standard idiomatic expression in English is to do something '**for a reason**' or '**for several reasons**.' 
• Options 1, 2, and 3 do not logically or grammatically fit the context of providing a reason for an action. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**. **Complete Sentence:** *'The CEO decided to quit the job **for**__ several reasons.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: 'about'** is generally used to indicate a subject or a topic (e.g., a conversation **about** work). It does not correctly link a decision to its underlying reasons in this sentence structure. 
• **Option 2: 'with'** usually indicates accompaniment, manner, or possession (e.g., writing **with** a pen), which is not applicable here. 
• **Option 3: 'of'** expresses a relationship between a part and a whole or belonging (e.g., the name **of** the company). It is grammatically incorrect to use 'of' to introduce the reasons for quitting in this context. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
The poor villagers are unable to cope up with the rising cost of living.

options.text: not able to cope up with

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**unable to cope with**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The phrase **cope with** is a standard **English phrasal verb** that means to deal effectively with something difficult, to manage a stressful situation, or to endure a hardship.

• The usage of **cope up with** is a common **grammatical error** often found in Indian English, likely resulting from a confusion between the two distinct idioms **cope with** and **keep up with**.

• In formal **linguistic structures**, the preposition **up** is considered redundant and incorrect when paired with **cope**; the verb **cope** is intransitive and traditionally only takes the preposition **with** to connect to its object.

• The sentence requires the removal of the unnecessary word **up** to ensure **syntactic precision**, making **unable to cope with** the only grammatically sound replacement for the underlined segment.

• The context of the sentence involves the struggle of **poor villagers** against the **rising cost of living**, which refers to an **inflationary pressure** or economic challenge that one must manage or endure.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Cope with** vs. **Keep up with**:

• **Cope with**: Focuses on the **psychological** or **physical capacity** to handle a burden or a difficult task (e.g., coping with grief or financial loss).

• **Keep up with**: Focuses on **maintaining the same pace**, level, or progress as another entity (e.g., keeping up with the neighbors or keeping up with the news).

• **Redundancy in Phrasal Verbs**:

• Many errors in competitive examinations involve **superfluous prepositions**. Just as **cope** does not require **up**, verbs like **await** do not require **for**, and **comprise** does not require **of** in the active voice.

• The word **cope** originates from the **Old French** word **couper** (to strike or cut), evolving in English to signify a successful 'contending' or 'struggle' against something.

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

The minister's speech was full of __facile promises that seemed to appease the crowds,__ but insiders know they are unlikely to ever be fulfilled.

options.text: aggravating promises that seemed to placate the crowds
frugal promises that seemed to facilitate the crowds
fervent promises that seemed to enervate the crowds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No improvement required**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence is grammatically and semantically accurate as it stands, making use of the adjective **facile** to describe the **minister's promises**.

• The term **facile** refers to something that is **superficial** or simplistic, often ignoring the true complexities of a situation. In political rhetoric, **facile promises** are those made easily to sound appealing but lack genuine substance or a practical plan for execution.

• The verb **appease**, which means to **pacify** or satisfy someone by meeting their demands or desires, correctly describes the intended effect of the speech on the **crowds**.

• The phrase **insiders know they are unlikely to ever be fulfilled** provides the necessary context to justify the use of **facile**, indicating that the commitments were shallow and unrealistic.

• Therefore, the original wording perfectly captures the contrast between the public **rhetoric** and the private reality known to **insiders**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Analysis of incorrect terminology in options:**

• **Aggravating vs. Placate**: **Aggravating** means making a problem or situation worse, which is the **semantic opposite** of the goal to **placate** or calm a crowd.

• **Frugal**: This term describes someone who is **economical** or sparing with money or food; it is contextually inappropriate for describing the nature of a **minister's speech**.

• **Facilitate**: This means to make an action or process **easier**, but it does not fit the context of satisfying or managing a **crowd's emotions**.

• **Fervent vs. Enervate**: While **fervent** means having **passionate intensity**, the verb **enervate** means to **weaken** or drain someone of energy. A fervent speech is designed to inspire, not to **enervate** the audience.

</ul

• **Example: **It would be **sensible** to carry an **extra set of keys** just in case you **lose** one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **A very good and honest person**. **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **To plan ahead** (आगे की योजना बनाना): To think about and make arrangements for the **future**. • **Example:** If you want your business to succeed, you must learn **to plan ahead** for potential market changes. • **To travel far** (दूर की यात्रा करना): To go on a journey to a **distant place**. • **Example:** In his youth, he used **to travel far** across the globe to explore different cultures. • **To speak indirectly** (घुमा-फिराकर बात करना): To avoid getting to the main point, often referred to as **beating around the bush**. • **Example:** Instead of being honest about the mistake, he started **to speak indirectly** to avoid taking blame. 40:Tc5b, The correct answer is **Option 1**.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. The Sun gives us light and warmth every day. 

P. It helps plants grow and make food. 

Q. It gives energy to all living things. 

R. The Sun controls the weather and seasons. 

S. Without the Sun, life on Earth cannot exist. 

6. The Sun is truly the source of life on Earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The passage explores the vital role of the **Sun** in sustaining various forms of existence on **Earth**, moving from specific biological processes to broader environmental impacts. 
• **Sentence 1** introduces the topic by mentioning the **Sun** and the basic benefits it provides: **light and warmth**. 
• **Sentence P** is the first logical step in the sequence as it describes how **plants** use that **light** to grow and produce **food** through photosynthesis. 
• **Sentence Q** follows, extending this idea to explain that the **Sun** is the ultimate provider of **energy** to **all living things** (since plants form the base of the food chain). 
• **Sentence R** transitions to the physical role of the **Sun**, explaining how its warmth controls the **weather and seasons** across the globe. 
• **Sentence S** serves as a final summarizing point of the intermediate section, stating that without the **Sun**, **life on Earth** could not exist. 
• The sequence ends with **Sentence 6**, which reinforces the main theme that the **Sun** is the **source of life**. 
• The correct logical sequence is **PQRS**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'The **Sun** gives us **light and warmth** every day. It helps **plants grow** and make **food**. It gives **energy** to **all living things**. The **Sun** controls the **weather and seasons**. Without the **Sun**, **life on Earth** cannot exist. The **Sun** is truly the **source of life** on **Earth**.'</div

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. Discipline first helps us develop good habits in daily life. 

P. It teaches us to manage our time wisely and avoid laziness. 

Q. With discipline, we stay focused on our goals without distractions. 

R. It makes us responsible for our actions and decisions. 

S. Discipline improves our performance in studies, work, and personal life. 

6. Finally, it leads us to success and earns respect from others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The passage discusses the role of **discipline** in personal development and success. It follows a logical progression from **habits** to **actions** and finally to **outcomes**.
 
• **Sentence 1** introduces the central idea: **Discipline** helps develop **good habits** in daily life.
 
• **Sentence P follows sentence 1** because it provides immediate examples of the **good habits** mentioned: 
 
 
• 'It teaches us to **manage our time** wisely and **avoid laziness**.'
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows P** as it describes the mental state resulting from effective time management and lack of laziness: 
 
 
• 'With discipline, we stay **focused on our goals** without distractions.'
 
 
 
• **Sentence R follows Q** by shifting the focus to **internal character development** and accountability: 
 
 
• 'It makes us **responsible** for our actions and decisions.'
 
 
 
• **Sentence S follows R** as it shows the collective impact of focus and responsibility on practical aspects of life: 
 
 
• 'Discipline improves our **performance** in studies, work, and personal life.'
 
 
 
• **Sentence 6 concludes** the passage by stating the final rewards of this improved performance: **success** and **respect**.
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'**Discipline** first helps us develop **good habits** in daily life. It teaches us to **manage our time** wisely and **avoid laziness**. With discipline, we stay **focused on our goals** without distractions. It makes us **responsible** for our actions and decisions. Discipline improves our **performance** in studies, work, and personal life. Finally, it leads us to **success** and earns **respect** from others.'</div
